question.text: In an examination, there are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn></math> multiple choice questions with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn></math> choices, out of which exactly one is correct. There are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn></math> marks for each correct answer, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></math> marks for each wrong answer and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn></math> mark if the question is not attempted. Then, the number of ways a student appearing in the examination gets <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn></math> marks is _____

solution.text:
Let the marks obtained in each of the five MCQ be x1, x2, x3, x4, x5

Now, x1+x2+x3+x4+x5=5

Only one possibility satisfies the above equation i.e.  3,3,3,-2,-2

Hence, total number of ways =5!3!2!×2×2=40
